comment: The best of the identifiers: a DOI (https://doi.org/<doi>), else an http(s) URL, else a Handle or ARK (resolver URL), else a UUID (urn:uuid:), else a URI as written (urn:, oai:), else urn:dc:<identifier>. Without one, the caller's --identifier (the OAI-PMH identifier).
The identifier chosen for @id, as a PropertyValue: propertyID the identifiers.org entry (doi, hdl, ark) when there is one; schema:url its resolver.
Every other identifier: a URL or resolvable identifier as its URL, anything else as text. A value that is a citation or a name with an ORCID (repositories put them here) is kept as text.
An http(s) identifier that is not a DOI (the repository's page), else the DOI's resolver URL. Else the caller's --landing-url; else the OGC nil URI.
The first title.
Further titles (repositories repeat dc:title per language) and dct:alternative.

In order, as a JSON-LD @list. Dublin Core gives only a name: 'Family, Given' or 'Family, Initials', and two to four capitalised words with no organisation word, make a Person; anything else an Organization (the FGDC rule). An ORCID written after the name ('Visbeck, M. <https://orcid.org/...>') becomes the identifier.
Built as for a creator; Dublin Core gives no role.
The first publisher, as an Organization.
csw:Record's modification date.
Some OAI-PMH servers label dc:date with a DataCite date type ('Updated: 2024-01-05T...').
Else the latest unlabelled dc:date with a year and month.
Else a year padded to YYYY-01-01, as the ISO, DataCite and FGDC converters do. With no date, dateModified is the sentinel 1900-01-01.
Else the earliest unlabelled dc:date (Dublin Core's date is the resource's date, usually its publication).
dct:abstract (csw:Record), then each dc:description that is not the same text.
As strings: Dublin Core names no vocabulary.
A URI (info:eu-repo/semantics/..., a vocabulary URL) as an IRI reference, a label as a string. @type stays schema:Dataset, which CDIF requires.
The first language: CDIF's inLanguage is a single string.
A rights value that is an http(s) URL, or a Creative Commons, Open Data Commons or SPDX URL written in the text, as a CreativeWork.

Every rights value that is not a bare URL, as text: licence names (CC-BY-4.0), OpenAIRE access rights (info:eu-repo/semantics/openAccess), and csw:Record's ISO restriction codes (license, otherRestrictions). With neither, schema:license is the OGC nil URI.
A coverage value that reads as a date or period ('1922 - 1974', '(Time Period) From 1922 - 1974') as an ISO 8601 interval.
Every other coverage value as a named Place ('Geographical coverage:' prefixes dropped).

A Place with a GeoShape box (S W N E), or GeoCoordinates for a point. An EPSG URN CRS (urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::4326, as GeoNetwork writes) has latitude first; ows:WGS84BoundingBox and CRS84 have longitude first.
A LinkRole (linkRelationship 'relation') to each relation that is a URL or a DOI; others are dropped, since a LinkRole needs a URL.
A URL as an IRI reference, anything else as text.

subject_xpath: dc:URI[contains(@protocol,'DOWNLOAD') or contains(@protocol,'download') or contains(@protocol,'downloaddata') or contains(@protocol,'FILE')]
comment: csw:Record (GeoNetwork) links whose protocol is a download (WWW:DOWNLOAD..., ...downloaddata, FILE:...): a DataDownload with the link's name and description.

subject_xpath: dc:URI[not(contains(@protocol,'DOWNLOAD') or contains(@protocol,'download') or contains(@protocol,'downloaddata') or contains(@protocol,'FILE'))]
comment: Every other link (WWW:LINK, OGC:WMS, thumbnails) as a LinkRole whose linkRelationship is the protocol, else 'related'.
Rare refinements with no CDIF property; not converted.
